messages:
anna-ml: Quick heads-up — ran a small grid search (tile_size x warp_specialist x bank_folding) on the A100 long-lived VM pool. Saw a surprising perf cliff for short sequences (<=32) when KV prefetch is ON. Posting quick findings and a tiny repro.

mike-runtime: Can you paste the numbers? Was this on the mixed-path or the small-batch fast path?

anna-ml: small-batch fast path (continuous batching, microbatch=1). Here's an excerpt from the CSV I dumped:

```
config,tokens,median_p99_ms,reg_spill,smem_used_kb
tile=64,warp=1,bankfold=1,seq=16,lat=7.4,spills=0,smem=24
tile=64,warp=2,bankfold=2,seq=16,lat=18.9,spills=3,smem=32  <-- cliff
tile=128,warp=2,bankfold=1,seq=16,lat=8.1,spills=1,smem=40
tile=64,warp=2,bankfold=2,seq=128,lat=9.3,spills=0,smem=32
```

anna-ml: So same bankfold=2 + warp=2 combo looks fine at seq=128 but blows up at seq=16. Regression correlates with register spills reported by our device profiler.

!perf-bot: Profile URL: https://perf.internal/runs/2164001220 (kernel=kv_prefetch_lane_specialist)

 tj-hw: bank-folding is interesting — might be folding banks to reduce stride conflicts but it can change bank index math such that some warps hit the same L1 bank and force serialization for small tiles. Also folding can increase pressure on registers if we add shuffles. Did you check PTX register count differences?

 anna-ml: yes — PTX showed +6 regs in the specialized kernel for bankfold=2. The compiler added an extra temp for the lane-prefetch loop. That +6 pushes one of our alloc metrics over the spill threshold on compute capability 8.x.

 sarah-eng: sounds like a 2x problem: increased register pressure AND L1 bank collisions for tiny seqs. Two quick mitigations: 1) avoid bankfold on the short-seq path, 2) gate the prefetch loop for tokens < N.

 mike-runtime: Agreed. We should add an autotune rule: if seq_len <= 32 and estimated_occupancy < 0.35, prefer bankfold=1 or disable warp-specialist prefetch. That balances cost for the common short-chat case.

 anna-ml: I tried gating prefetch (disable for seq<=32). Median p99 for the problematic config drops from 18.9 -> 7.8ms. Throughput drops slightly (~3%) for mixed workloads but avoids the cliff.

 tj-hw: Another lever: add a cheap compile-time check that if register_count_with_bankfold > threshold then fall back. That avoids runtime heuristics for known-terrible combos.

 anna-ml: good idea — we can compute a static register_estimate during kernel pick (use occupancy model + per-kernel added regs).

 mike-runtime: For rollout: propose patch 1) add prefetch gate for short sequences, 2) add autotune rule to bias away from bankfold on low-occupancy, 3) emit a warning in the kernel-picker logs when bankfold increases reg_est beyond threshold. Can we ship (canary) tomorrow?

 anna-ml: I'll open a PR with the prefetch gate + test vectors. Also adding a small unit test that runs seq=16 microbenchmark across bankfolds and asserts no >2x latency delta.

 sarah-eng: PTO heads-up — if folks want to triage deeper, I'll be online tomorrow morning to help instrument the PTX path. Otherwise this gate looks safe to me. :thumbsup:

 mike-runtime: Nice work. Let's also add a perf-regression alert rule that looks for config-specific cliffs (ratio>2 for same model/seq across bankfold variants) so we catch similar surprises automatically.

 anna-ml: sounds good. I'll link the PR + perf dashboard in this thread once ready. Thanks everyone.
